run.question:
Our US prod cluster is having a checkout incident — investigate using
app-262-prod-logs.

report.summary: US-prod evidence exists only as 5 log documents in app-262-prod-logs; the three that carry cluster=production-us-east-1 are ERRORs describing one payment-failure chain: checkout-service 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)' at 2026-11-21T03:56:51Z, payment-service 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 2026-11-21T04:56:51Z, and checkout-service 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)' at 2026-11-21T05:26:51Z. The two 'Healthy' INFO lines in the same index carry cluster=production-eu-west-1 and therefore say nothing about the US cluster. Prometheus and Jaeger were SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt, so error rates, latency trends, span-level call edges and the start of any deviation could not be measured; no latency trend is claimed without a baseline. The Kubernetes cluster reachable in this Run is a single-node cluster (node opspilot-m1-control-plane, Ready) whose otel-demo namespace holds checkout and payment deployments at 1/1 ready with populated Service endpoints; all its containers stopped at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (exit 255, reason Unknown) and restarted 04:23:48-04:24:24, and its checkout container logged 'payment went through' transactions up to 05:56:20Z with no error lines in window. Nothing in the Kubernetes objects carries a cluster/region identity matching production-us-east-1, and the service/log formats differ from the app-262-prod-logs records, so that cluster cannot be confirmed as the affected environment. Hypotheses remaining: the deepest named dependency is the external payment provider 'Stripe-US' (log text only), and an intervening network/DNS path toward that provider is an unresolved alternative. Flagd fault-injection settings for payment exist but read as off when observed. Conclusion is partial: the failure chain in the US-prod logs is evidenced, but no in-cluster object is identified as the origin of the fault and the trigger of the upstream timeouts is unknown.

claims.text: app-262-prod-logs holds 5 documents in the authorized window; three are ERROR records with cluster=production-us-east-1 from checkout-service and payment-service at 2026-11-21T03:56:51Z, 04:56:51Z and 05:26:51Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)', 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms', and 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)'.

The two INFO records at 2026-11-21T04:56:51Z ('Healthy: p95 latency 230ms') and 2026-11-21T05:26:51Z ('Healthy: success rate 99.7%') carry cluster=production-eu-west-1, a different cluster from the US one, so they are not evidence about production-us-east-1.
The index app-262-prod-logs maps only cluster, level, message, service and timestamp fields and held 5 documents / 7.2kb with health green at query time.

The Kubernetes cluster reachable in this Run has a single node named opspilot-m1-control-plane with Ready=True, MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure=False, and no region/zone or cluster-name label that can be compared with production-us-east-1.

In that cluster, namespace otel-demo runs an 'otel-demo' application: deployments checkout and payment each report 1 ready / 1 available of 1 replica, alongside frontend, cart, currency, email, flagd, kafka-less demo services, jaeger, kube-state-metrics, prometheus and load-generator.

Every otel-demo pod has restartCount 1 with lastState.terminated.reason=Unknown and exitCode=255: for cart, checkout, payment and valkey-cart the previous container finishedAt is exactly 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z and the current containers started 2026-11-21T04:23:48Z-04:24:24Z, while the pod startTime remains 2026-11-20T16:32, i.e. containers restarted in place under unchanged pod identities.

The otel-demo flagd container shut down at 2026-11-21T04:07:51Z and its replacement started at 04:23:49Z, relaunching from the same local flag file ./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json (filepath sync watcher, IResolver on port 8013).

The flagd-config ConfigMap in otel-demo defines the fault-injection settings productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%'), paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad; at the time of reading, every flag's defaultVariant was 'off' and no targeting rules were present.

The payment deployment runs image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment with env FLAGD_HOST=flagd/FLAGD_PORT=8013 and no payment-failure or unreachable env setting; the checkout deployment runs ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout with PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080; both deployments are at generation 1.

The otel-demo payment Service (ClusterIP, port 8080) and checkout Service (ClusterIP, port 8080) both have populated endpoints (payment 10.244.0.17, checkout 10.244.0.12), so service-to-pod wiring was not empty at query time.
The payment container logged 'Charge request received.' entries continuously up to 2026-11-21T05:56:20.795Z in this cluster's pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d.

The checkout container logged successful order flow in this cluster, including '[PlaceOrder]', 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' and 'order confirmation email sent' at 05:54:09Z, 05:54:59Z, 05:56:08Z and 05:56:20Z.

The 18 events in the authorized window all involve namespace app-101 and are Normal: deployment loki scaled up a ReplicaSet 0->1 at 05:49:42Z, pod loki-66445c6d6f-6sxbh was scheduled/pulled/created/started, and pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-xm8b2 was created at 05:50:06Z and its containers 'payment-api' and 'promtail' stopped at 05:50:19Z; no event involves a pod, deployment or service in otel-demo.

The checkout incident in the US cluster traces to the external payment provider 'Stripe-US': payment-service's charge call to stripe-us /v1/charges timed out after 30000ms, which surfaced as the 30s payment-provider timeout on POST /api/checkout and then as the checkout circuit breaker opening for payment-service at a 44% failure rate. Only log text names this dependency; no metrics or spans were available to confirm it.

A remaining alternative candidate is an in-path fault on the network/DNS route between payment-service and the Stripe-US endpoint (30s connect/response stalls can also come from packet loss or resolution failures); the evidence cannot separate provider-side slowness from a client-side connectivity fault because traces, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_* and http_server_request_duration_seconds_* readings were unobtainable.

A switched-on flagd fault flag for payment being the cause of the observed checkout failure is not supported: in the flagd-config ConfigMap read during this Run both payment-relevant flags (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable) and all other flags have defaultVariant 'off' with no targeting rules, and the payment/checkout deployments carry no payment-fault env setting. The observed state is at query time, so the flag state during the incident remains unknown.

The container restart of all otel-demo pods is rejected as the cause of the reported checkout incident: the termination at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z hit unrelated containers in the same instant (cart, valkey-cart as well as checkout and payment) with exitCode 255 and reason Unknown, pod identities were unchanged, the US-prod checkout timeout record at 03:56:51Z precedes it, and checkout logged 'payment went through' after the restart through 05:56:20Z.

The app-101 workload churn around 05:49-05:50Z is rejected as the cause of the checkout failures: those events are Normal Scheduling/Pulling/Created/Started/SuccessfulCreate and ScalingReplicaSet for deployment loki and pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-xm8b2 in a different namespace, with no event touching otel-demo checkout or payment.

The Kubernetes cluster readable in this Run does not itself show the reported checkout failure: its checkout and payment deployments are 1/1 ready, both Services have endpoints, and checkout logged successful 'payment went through' transactions up to 05:56:20Z. This cluster is therefore not evidence of impact and cannot be confirmed to be production-us-east-1.

Advisory: obtain the actual error-rate and latency series for checkout-service and payment-service in production-us-east-1 (traces_span_metrics_calls_total by status_code, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count by rpc_grpc_status_code, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count) once Prometheus is reachable, so the deviation start and the 44% failure rate can be verified rather than taken from a log line.

Advisory: check the Stripe-US provider status and the network path/DNS resolution from payment-service to the stripe-us /v1/charges endpoint for the 03:56-05:26Z period, and confirm which cluster identity the app-262-prod-logs records belong to, since the reachable Kubernetes cluster carries no matching region/cluster name.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable on every attempt (execute_prometheus_instant_query for 'up' and for count by (namespace) (kube_pod_info), get_all_labels, get_metric_names, list_prometheus_rules, get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so error-rate, request-rate and latency series (traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_*, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count) are unknown, not zero; no latency trend can be stated and no alert rule state could be read.

Jaeger was unreachable (traces_list_services and traces_search for service 'checkout' both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no spans exist for this Run: parent-child call edges between checkout and payment and span-level timeouts are unknown.

Whether the reachable Kubernetes cluster (single node opspilot-m1-control-plane, namespace otel-demo) is the 'US prod cluster' named in the question could not be verified: the objects carry no cluster or region field matching production-us-east-1, and the app-262-prod-logs records use service names 'checkout-service'/'payment-service' and messages ('Stripe-US', 'Circuit-breaker open') that do not appear in the otel-demo pod logs. No Kubernetes object is therefore attributed to the incident.

The exact start of the deviation in production-us-east-1 is unknown: app-262-prod-logs returned only 5 documents in the whole window (3 US ERRORs, 2 EU INFOs), so counts, rates and background-error levels could not be derived, and nothing shows whether errors existed before 03:56:51Z.

What triggered the container restarts in the reachable cluster is unknown: all containers terminated at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exitCode 255 and reason Unknown under unchanged pod templates, no otel-demo event survived (events only span 05:28:04Z-05:50:19Z and all belong to app-101), and no fault setting was seen switched on, so this change cannot be placed as affected or as changed for another reason.

Queries for networkpolicies, resourcequotas and ingresses in the reachable cluster returned no data (status no_data), so the absence of a NetworkPolicy, quota or Ingress misconfiguration is unverified rather than confirmed.

Payment and checkout pod-log queries for error/timeout/stripe patterns in the reachable cluster returned no matching lines (status no_data), so the absence of such log lines there is unconfirmed; additionally 6 matching lines in the checkout container and 4 in the payment container fell after the authorized window end (05:56:59Z) and could not be read.

The change_history integration is not integrated, so no change, deploy or configuration edit record exists for either cluster; who or what caused the Stripe-US timeouts and whether anything was changed during the window is unknown.
Secrets were not readable, so any credential or provider endpoint configuration used by payment-service could not be checked.
next_steps: Restore Prometheus and Jaeger access for target m0-otel-20260909, then query error rate and latency for checkout-service and payment-service in production-us-east-1 over 2026-11-21T03:00Z-05:57Z to establish the deviation start and confirm the 44% failure rate.
Confirm the cluster identity of the app-262-prod-logs records with the platform team, and confirm whether the otel-demo workloads in the reachable cluster belong to the same environment.
Check the external Stripe-US provider status page and payment-service's egress path/DNS for 2026-11-21T03:56Z-05:26Z, since the only named upstream is stripe-us /v1/charges.
Review change history out-of-band for the US prod cluster in the window; the change_history integration was unavailable in this Run.
